project_specification.project_name: nullius — feature 248 (System loops policy selection until no batch is selected or the round cap is reached, which returns the revealed set)
project_specification.addition_summary:
Implement app_spec.xml feature 248 in the existing replay member (packages/replay, import name replay; seat src/app/modules/replay): the outer loop of docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md §10.1's `replay()`, the part feature 245's own plan explicitly cedes — "The loop, the round cap and the 'no batch selected' termination are feature 248's; this module owns one step." Feature 248 declares `depends_on=245`, and it is the loop that drives 245's transition:
revealed = {tree.root} rounds = 0 while rounds < K2: # the cap is 248's batch = policy.select(prefix_view(revealed)) # prefix-only if not batch: # no batch → terminate break for v in batch: child = tree.child_of(v) # 245's transition if child: revealed.add(child) rounds += 1 return revealed # the revealed set
One new module, replay/rounds.py, and one verb — `run_replay(select, question, tree, *, round_cap)`. It is the runtime's half of §10.1's asymmetry: 245 is one step (`child = tree.child_of(v)`), and 248 is the loop that takes those steps until the policy stops selecting or the round cap is hit, then hands back the revealed set. It does not select, does not score, does not commit — those are the policy's (the `select` it is handed), feature 249's and feature 250's — and it does not re-derive a recorded child: it drives 245's `ReplayTransition`, which is what `depends_on=245` means structurally.
(1) The loop. `run_replay` opens 245's transition at the tree's roots (`ReplayTransition.over(tree)` — the prefix seeded at the parentless nodes, exactly 245's `{tree.root}`), then repeats: build the policy's prefix from the transition's revealed set, ask the policy for a batch, and — when a batch comes back — advance the transition by each selected node's recorded child, one `transition(v)` per element, until either the policy returns no batch or the round cap is reached. It returns the revealed set as 245 reports it (`transition.prefix()`, ascending, §12's ordering rule), never a count, a score or a commit — the sentence names one return, "the revealed set", and a loop that returned more would be wearing feature 249's or 250's verb. Termination is the disjunction the sentence states: `if not batch: break` (no batch selected — feature 3/242's "the policy has selected no batch", the empty list `legal_actions` hands a leaf) OR `rounds >= round_cap` (the cap). Both are tested; a loop that honored only one would either run forever on a policy that always selects, or stop one round short of a policy that would have selected again.
(2) The two collaborators arrive duck-typed, because a member never imports another member — not even its own past, and not the policy-runtime member whose `PolicyQuestion` and authored-policy `select` the loop drives. The seam therefore reads what each collaborator *is*, never `isinstance`s it (the module loader imports a member under a synthetic name and re-executes it, so the composed `PolicyQuestion` this process hands out is a second class object of the same name):
* **`select`** — the callable shape of `policy.select(prefix_view(...))`. The loop never names `prefix_view` or a `Policy` (it owns neither and may not import them); the caller wires the closure — `lambda q: policy.select(prefix_view(q))` — and hands the callable in. The loop calls `select(question)` once per round and treats a falsy answer as termination. `select` is validated callable **before the tree is opened and before the first round runs**: a non-callable is refused, because a loop that opened a transition and read a tree and then discovered it had no policy to call would have spent the walk it was meant to guard against spending — the same ordering 245's generator refusal and 251's loader refusal hold (a refusal that ran first would have spent the thing it was refusing to spend). * **`question`** — the read-side question (feature 217's `PolicyQuestion`, the object `prefix_view` is built over). The loop reads exactly one verb off it — `probe_batch` — and nothing else. It does not build a prefix view (223's), does not read `observed`/`legal_actions`/`meta`/`budget` (the policy's, through the surface the caller supplies), and does not reveal on the policy's behalf (220's). It syncs the question's reveal set to the transition's revealed set, and that is the whole of its demand on the question. A carrier with no callable `probe_batch` is refused in the member's vocabulary, naming what arrived.
(3) The reveal-set reconciliation — the load-bearing detail, and the reason the loop touches the question at all. The transition and the question are two objects over one tree, each holding its own reveal set: 245's transition grows `revealed` by the recorded child; 217's question grows its reveal set by `probe_batch`. `prefix_view(question)` exposes only `question.observed()` — the question's reveal set — so the policy sees the prefix the question has revealed, not the prefix the transition has. If the two sets drift, the policy is shown a frontier the walk is not standing on. The loop is the reconciler: it seeds the question with the roots once (`question.probe_batch(transition.prefix())`, so the policy's first view is the seeded prefix), and after each round it reveals into the question **exactly the children the transition newly revealed** — the non-`None` returns of that round's `transition(v)` calls — by one `probe_batch(newly)`. It does not re-probe the whole prefix each round: `probe_batch` is idempotent and all-or-nothing (a duplicate is one cell, the whole call runs ascending, a batch naming a node the tree does not hold reveals none of them), so re-probing would be correct but quadratic in the campaign's nodes across the rounds — the very cost 245 refuses on its side (per-step re-derivation measured at 76 ms for a 500-node campaign against 252's 50 ms budget). Revealing only the new children keeps the question's reveal set equal to the transition's revealed set at every `select`, in O(N) over the whole walk rather than O(rounds × N). The reconciliation reads `probe_batch`'s contract, it does not restate it: a node the transition revealed is a node the tree holds (245 adds only recorded children, and refuses a tree that records several at construction), so the sync never hands `probe_batch` a node outside the tree, and `probe_batch`'s own all-or-nothing validation is the second statement of a fact the transition already guarantees.
(4) The round cap — `K2`, and it is a **required argument, validated as a positive integer, with no default and no module constant**. docs §10.1 writes `while rounds < K2` with `K2` a symbolic bound, never a number, and the repository's recorded hard constraints forbid an absolute target (prd §436: "no absolute score targets"; the admission gate 230 refuses a policy with a hardcoded cap). So the cap is the caller's policy decision — a deployment chooses how many selection rounds a replay may take — and this module spells no number for it. `round_cap` is refused when it is not a positive integer (a `bool`, a zero, a negative, a non-int) **before the transition is opened**, because a cap that is not a positive count names no loop: zero or negative would terminate before a single round (a silent no-op that reads as a completed replay), and a non-int would break the `rounds < round_cap` comparison. The refusal names the value and that the cap is a positive round count. This module is deliberately the *only* place a round count is compared, so the cap cannot be restated at a second `while` elsewhere in the member.
(5) One new error SIBLING under `ReplayError`, split by the repair the caller must make: `ReplayRoundError` — the round loop's ask is malformed, and the repair is on the caller's side of the call (pass a callable `select`, a positive `round_cap`, a question that fronts the campaign). It carries the three refusals the loop owns — the non-callable `select`, the non-positive `round_cap`, the carrier with no `probe_batch` — because they share one repair (fix the argument handed to `run_replay`) and a caller's single `except ReplayError` must catch every way the loop's ask can fail, the discipline `replay.errors` states for the tree, the residence and the report. It is **not** a child of `ReplayTreeError`: a malformed ask to the loop is a different repair from a stored tree no transition can walk, and a caller skipping a bad tree must not silently skip the refusal that says the loop was handed no callable policy. A malformed *tree*, by contrast, still surfaces as 245's `ReplayTreeError` — the loop opens the transition and lets its refusal propagate, because the tree's unfitness is a statement about the tree, repaired at the store, not a statement about the loop's arguments.
(6) The composed spelling — `ReplayEngine.run(select, question, *, round_cap)` on 245's stateless facade, reached through the component the member registers under `replay`. It resolves the deployment's campaign tree (`self.tree()`, the call-time resolution 245 already owns, never at composition — the recursion the facade's docstring argues) and delegates to `run_replay`. The import of `run_replay` is deferred into the method body, not at module top: `rounds.py` imports `ReplayTransition` from `transition.py`, so a top-level `from .rounds import run_replay` in `transition.py` would close an import cycle; the deferred import is the same seam `resolve_tree` takes (`importlib.import_module` inside the function) and keeps `transition.py` import-cheap at composition. No second `replay` component, no `replay-`-prefixed sibling — the loop's behaviour is added to the facade, the law the package `__init__` states (one component per member name).
**What this module deliberately is not.** It is not the selector: `select` is the caller's closure over the policy and `prefix_view`, and a loop that chose the batch would be a runtime making the policy's decision — the exact overreach 245's docstring refuses ("a transition that chose what to reveal would be a runtime making the policy's decision"). It is not feature 249's commit — the loop returns the revealed set and stops; the committed pick `policy.commit()` and the negative-infinity-on-none are 249's, over this loop's return. It is not feature 250's scoring, not feature 222's score, not feature 255's `replay_score` row — the loop measures no score and persists nothing. It is not 245's transition — it drives it, one step per selected node, and does not re-derive a recorded child. It is not the prefix-only barrier (223's view, 224's answer surface, 225's armed guard): the loop trusts that `select` returns a prefix-only batch — the barrier enforces that, at the surface and the guard, not here — and does not re-police which nodes the batch names; a batch element the tree does not hold is refused by 245's `transition(v)`, not by a second barrier minted in the loop. It holds no store, opens no database, consults no clock, and is pure over the tree and the two collaborators it is handed — the §12 determinism contract, restated for the loop: two replays of one policy on one tree are one revealed set.
No central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings or migration is edited; no table is created or written; no new `@register` component is added (245's single `replay` component is untouched, the facade gains a verb). The member joins by workspace-scan convention and does not import another workspace member — the tree and the question are consumed duck-typed, and `select`/`prefix_view`/`policy` are the caller's. The module is stdlib-only: `collections.abc`, `typing`.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace (packages/* members, import names are underscored slugs) / pytest (ruff + mypy conventions). The module loader (src/app/module_loader.py) discovers members from the root pyproject.toml `[tool.uv.workspace] members = ["packages/*"]`, imports each package so its module-level `@register` fires, and composes what each `@register` builder contributes under a component name. `app` (src/app) is a namespace package with no `__init__.py`; the seats in src/app/modules/<member>/ are reached by namespace import (e.g. app.modules.replay). A member never imports another member — it reaches shared shapes through `app.*`, never through a sibling package's import name.
existing_context.test_baseline: The repository-level suite under tests/ is collected by pytest with testpaths=tests; each workspace member's own suite lives under packages/<member>/tests/ and is collected under its own conftest (same-basename files collide under one pytest run), and is NOT graded by the bare `uv run pytest` acceptance gate — a member suite must be run explicitly (run both `uv run pytest tests/` and the member's own `packages/replay/tests/`). The replay member suite baseline is the feature 245/251–254 suite already in packages/replay/tests. The repo lint is red on main (mypy absent, pre-existing ruff errors), so lint only the changed files and compare to a sibling. The replay member is stdlib-only, and feature 248 keeps it that way: collections.abc, typing.
existing_context.conventions: snake_case modules, one verb and its refusals per module, docstrings that cite the governing documents by section and quote the sentence they implement, refusals that name the subject and the repair, error classes split by the repair rather than by where the failure was noticed, and delegation rather than restatement wherever a sibling already owns the law (the recorded child to 245's transition, the reveal-set sync to `probe_batch`'s idempotency, the ordering to §12). The member's honesty stance: a module cites the document it implements and says what it is NOT (this one is not the selector, not the commit, not the score, not the transition, not the barrier; it is no component, holds nothing, persists nothing). The duck-typed seam validates what it reads rather than `isinstance`-ing the carrier, because the loader's synthetic module name makes a class check refuse a composed record.
existing_context.context: existing modules in packages/replay/src/replay/: errors.py (the member's vocabulary — ReplayError and its siblings ReplayTreeError, ChildGenerationRefused, ReplayReturnsError, ParquetReadRefused, ReplayMetricsError, RecomputationSuspectedError), transition.py (feature 245 — ReplayTransition, ReplayEngine, replay_transition, replay_roots, child_map, recorded_child; the transition owns the revealed set and the recorded-child step the loop drives), returns.py (251), duration.py (252), alert.py (253), metrics.py (254). The policy-runtime member's `PolicyQuestion.probe_batch` (feature 220) is the batch-reveal verb the loop's sync consumes — idempotent, all-or-nothing, ascending, returning only the cells newly revealed — reached duck-typed, never imported. Tests live in packages/replay/tests/ with their own conftest.py providing a duck-typed StoredTree/ StoredNode vocabulary and a `transition` fixture; the repo-level tests/replay/ suite pins the composed wiring over the real CampaignTree.

feature.description: System loops policy selection over one stored tree until no batch is selected or the round cap is reached, and returns the revealed set — the outer `while rounds < K2` loop of docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md §10.1's `replay()`, the part feature 245's plan cedes ("The loop, the round cap and the 'no batch selected' termination are feature 248's"). It exposes `run_replay(select, question, tree, *, round_cap)`: it opens feature 245's `ReplayTransition.over(tree)` (the prefix seeded at the tree's roots), then repeats — build the policy's prefix from the transition's revealed set, ask the caller-supplied `select(question)` for a batch, and when a batch comes back advance the transition by each selected node's recorded child (one `transition(v)` per element) — until either the policy returns no batch (`if not batch: break`, feature 3/242's "the policy has selected no batch") or `rounds >= round_cap`. It returns `transition.prefix()` (the revealed set, ascending, §12's ordering rule) and nothing else — no count, no score, no commit (those are the policy's `select`, feature 249's `commit` and feature 250/255's scoring). The two collaborators arrive duck-typed (a member never imports another member): `select` is the callable shape of `policy.select(prefix_view(...))` the caller wires as a closure, validated callable before the tree is opened; `question` is feature 217's read-side `PolicyQuestion`, read through exactly one verb, `probe_batch`, which the loop uses to keep the question's reveal set equal to the transition's revealed set so the policy is always shown the frontier the walk is standing on — seeding the roots once, then revealing only the children each round newly revealed (the non-`None` returns of that round's `transition(v)`), never re-probing the whole prefix (idempotent though `probe_batch` is, re-probing is O(rounds × N) where revealing the new children is O(N) over the walk — the per-step re-derivation cost 245 refuses). The round cap `K2` is a required argument, validated a positive integer, with no default and no module constant (docs §10.1's `K2` is a symbolic bound and the repository forbids an absolute target, prd §436); it is refused when not a positive integer (bool, zero, negative, non-int) before the transition is opened. One new error sibling under `ReplayError` — `ReplayRoundError`, for the loop's malformed ask (non-callable `select`, non-positive `round_cap`, a carrier with no callable `probe_batch`), never a child of `ReplayTreeError` (a malformed ask to the loop is a different repair from a stored tree no transition can walk); a malformed tree still surfaces as 245's `ReplayTreeError` through the loop. The composed spelling `ReplayEngine.run(select, question, *, round_cap)` on feature 245's stateless facade resolves the deployment's tree via `self.tree()` and delegates to `run_replay` through a method-body import (the import-cycle seam the facade's `resolve_tree` already takes). No new `@register` component (245's single `replay` facade gains a verb), no table, no write, no store, no clock; stdlib-only (`collections.abc`, `typing`).

System passes an end-to-end replay in which a stub policy that closes over the question's revealed set selects, per round, the frontier node whose recorded child the stub tree holds; `run_replay` drives feature 245's transition (never re-deriving a recorded child — the stub asserts the transition, not the tree, advanced), seeds the question with the roots, keeps the question's reveal set equal to `transition.prefix()` at every `select`, reveals each newly-recorded child into the question exactly once (a counting `probe_batch` double asserts no node is re-probed), terminates on no batch (a `select` returning `[]` stops the walk and returns the current prefix) and on the round cap (a `select` that always returns a batch stops at exactly `round_cap` rounds with a frontier remaining), returns the revealed set ascending, is idempotent (a `select` that re-selects an already-revealed node reveals nothing new and does not double-count), and refuses a non-callable `select`, a non-positive `round_cap` (bool, zero, negative, non-int, each naming the value) and a carrier with no callable `probe_batch` before the transition is opened (a watched tree is never addressed), every refusal a `ReplayRoundError` and not a `ReplayTreeError`; a malformed tree still surfaces as 245's `ReplayTreeError`; and the loop over the real `CampaignTree` with a stub policy closing over `prefix_view(question)` proves the duck-typed seam matches the composed question and the reveal-set reconciliation holds end to end.

deliverables.deliverable: packages/replay/src/replay/rounds.py — the round loop and its refusals, with `run_replay(select, question, tree, *, round_cap)` in `__all__`. The loop opens 245's `ReplayTransition.over(tree)`, seeds the question's reveal set with the roots, then loops `select(question)` to a batch, advances the transition by each selected node's recorded child, syncs the question with the round's newly revealed children via one `probe_batch(newly)`, and terminates on no batch or the round cap, returning `transition.prefix()`. `select` validated callable, `round_cap` validated a positive int, and the question's `probe_batch` validated — all before the transition is opened. No `@register`, no table, no write, no store, no clock; the round cap carries no constant.

packages/replay/src/replay/errors.py — the `ReplayRoundError` sibling under `ReplayError`, added to `__all__`, for the round loop's malformed ask (non-callable `select`, non-positive `round_cap`, a carrier with no `probe_batch`); not a child of `ReplayTreeError`, argued in the module docstring by the repair.

packages/replay/src/replay/transition.py — the composed spelling `ReplayEngine.run(select, question, *, round_cap)`, resolving the deployment's tree via `self.tree()` and delegating to `run_replay` through a method-body import (the import-cycle seam the seat's `resolve_tree` already takes). No other change to 245's transition.
packages/replay/src/replay/__init__.py — export `run_replay` and `ReplayRoundError`; the member's one `@register` component stays 245's `replay` facade, which gains the `run` verb.

packages/replay/tests/test_rounds.py — the feature's own suite, against duck-typed doubles (a stub `select`, a stub question exposing only `probe_batch` over a reveal set, the StoredTree of conftest): the loop drives 245's transition (never re-deriving a recorded child — pinned by a `select` that asserts the transition, not the tree, advanced), the prefix seeded at the roots, the reveal set kept equal to the prefix at every `select` (the stub reads the question's `observed`-equivalent and the test asserts it matches `transition.prefix()`), termination on no batch (a `select` that returns `[]` stops the walk and returns the current prefix), termination on the round cap (a `select` that always returns a batch stops at exactly `round_cap` rounds even with a frontier remaining), the new-children sync revealing each node into the question exactly once (a counting `probe_batch` double asserts no node is re-probed — the anti-quadratic claim), the order of refusals (a non-callable `select`, a non-positive `round_cap`, and a carrier with no `probe_batch` each refused before the transition is opened — a watched tree is never addressed), `round_cap` validated a positive int (bool, zero, negative, non-int refused, each naming the value), every refusal a `ReplayRoundError` and not a `ReplayTreeError`, a malformed tree still surfacing as 245's `ReplayTreeError` through the loop, the revealed set returned ascending, and idempotence (a `select` that re-selects an already-revealed node reveals nothing new and does not double-count). test_errors.py extended with the sibling pin against the member's whole vocabulary; a repo-level tests/replay/ wiring test exercises the loop over the real CampaignTree with a stub policy closing over `prefix_view(question)`, proving the duck-typed seam matches the composed question and the reveal-set reconciliation holds end to end.
